clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11343 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 6085, Federal Register of April 18, 1967, signed April 12, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Long Island Rail Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, labor organizations (three disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 12, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by The Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 170 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 12, 1967. Thirty days after May 12, 1967 is June 11, 1967. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 12, 1967, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 11, 1967.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (32 FR 6085, the issue of April 18, 1967) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11343, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 12, 1967. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
